pages.title: About the lab
pages.content:
Lab

About the lab

About the lab

Hakuji Laboratory is a dental laboratory in Westmere, founded in 2009 by Ilse Marchetti. We make crowns, bridges and implant restorations for practices within courier reach.

One bench, seven people.

A small lab in Westmere

Hakuji Laboratory opened in 2009 at Unit 3, 18 Alder Yard, Westmere, so a small bench could stay with a case from the scan to the box that leaves the door. We work for dental practices. The accepted work is single crowns, bridges up to six units, veneers, inlays and onlays, implant crowns and night guards.

Full-arch implant bars, orthodontic appliances and full dentures sit outside that list. Design previews are prepared in the same room that mills and layers the work, and a practice can book a shade visit when a tooth has to be read beside its neighbours. Weekday courier pick-up links the practice to this address.

A new lab account is confirmed within one working day. Write to cases@hakuji-lab.example or use the account form, and we will reply with the confirmation or with the detail still missing.

A day at the bench

Monday to Friday

07:30The bench opens
10:30First courier pick-up
13:00Design previews sent for approval
16:00Second courier pick-up
18:00The lab closes

How a day runs

On Monday to Friday the bench opens at 07:30. The first courier pick-up is at 10:30. At 13:00 the design previews that are ready are sent out for approval.

The second pick-up is at 16:00, and the lab closes at 18:00. Saturday is open from 09:00 to 13:00 for shade visits by appointment only. Sunday is closed.

Pick-ups are the two weekday times, and both are included in the fees for practices inside the pick-up area. A scan follows the same clock. We send a design preview within two working days of receiving it.

After you approve the design we mill, finish and return the work by courier. A single crown is five working days, counted from the scan received or from the design approved. Bridges, veneers, implant crowns and night guards each keep the count published on the cases page.

The people at the bench

Seven people work the cases at this address.

Ilse Marchetti

Founder and ceramist, layering

She has layered porcelain here since she opened the lab in 2009, and a custom-shade crown still passes across her bench.

Daniel Okafor

CAD design lead

He prepares the design preview a practice approves before milling starts.

Mei-Lin Hsu

Implant restorations

She works on implant restorations, both screw-retained and cemented.

Tomas Varga

Milling and sintering

He runs milling and sintering, from the disc through to the finished unit.

Amara Nwosu

Shade visits and client care

She looks after shade visits and client care, including Saturday appointments from 09:00 to 13:00.

Sophie Laurent

Case intake and courier

She handles case intake and the courier, and meets the driver at 10:30 and at 16:00.

Rafael Ortiz

Guards and veneers

He makes night guards and veneers.

Materials on the bench

We work with zirconia, lithium disilicate, layering porcelain, PMMA, and hard and soft splint material. A monolithic zirconia crown is one line on the fee table. A layered zirconia crown is the custom-shade line, built with layering porcelain.

Lithium disilicate is used for a crown or a veneer. Inlays and onlays are ceramic. An implant crown includes the metal base.

Night guards are hard or dual-layer, made in the splint materials kept on the bench. PMMA is among the materials we work with. It has no separate line on the fee table, so we confirm it against the prescription before a case is booked in.

A shade visit at the lab is €35, for practices and their patients, by appointment. The shade room is here at Unit 3. Book it through the account page and mark the request as a shade visit.

ZirconiaLithium disilicateLayering porcelainPMMAHard and soft splint material

Send us your first case.

Open an account and we will set up your case link, your prescription form and a courier slot. Most practices send a first case within the week they open one, and we reply to every new account within one working day.

Open a lab account

pages.title: Accepted cases
pages.content:
Cases

Accepted work

Accepted cases

Six case types leave this bench, each with a material, a fee and a working-day count where we publish one. Send a scan or book a pick-up, then approve the design before we mill.

Six case types, one clear list.

case types

Six kinds of case

Single crowns

€95 monolithic · €145 layered · €125 lithium disilicate · 5 working days

Read the details

Bridges

€90 per unit · up to six units · 7 working days

Read the details

Veneers

€125 lithium disilicate · 6 working days

Read the details

Inlays and onlays

€110 ceramic · design preview within 2 working days

Read the details

Implant crowns

€210, metal base included · 8 working days

Read the details

Night guards

€70 hard or dual-layer · 4 working days

Read the details

In detail

What to send, per case type

Single crowns

A single crown is accepted in monolithic zirconia at €95, in layered zirconia with a custom shade at €145, or in lithium disilicate at €125. The lithium disilicate fee is the same figure used when the unit is a veneer, and veneer timing is listed on its own. Turnaround for a single crown is five working days, counted from the scan received or from the design approved.

Send the scan as STL, PLY, OBJ or DCM, or book a weekday courier for a physical impression. On the prescription, name the tooth, the material and the shade. We send a design preview within two working days, and milling starts after you approve it.

When a layered crown needs the shade read at the lab, book a shade visit. That visit is €35 and is a separate line from the crown.

Bridges

Bridges are accepted up to six units. The fee is €90 per unit for a zirconia bridge, so a four-unit bridge is four units on that line. Turnaround is seven working days, counted from the scan received or from the design approved.

Send one scan in STL, PLY, OBJ or DCM that includes the preparations the prescription names, or send an impression on the weekday courier. Write the number of units and the shade on the prescription, and keep the span within six units. The design preview is sent within two working days.

After approval, the bridge is milled, finished and returned by courier. A bridge request beyond six units is outside the work we accept. Full-arch implant bars are a separate exclusion, listed with the other work we do not take.

Veneers

Veneers are accepted as their own case type. The fee for a lithium disilicate crown or veneer is €125. Turnaround for veneers is six working days, counted from the scan received or from the design approved.

Rafael Ortiz finishes veneers at the bench. Send a scan in STL, PLY, OBJ or DCM, or a physical impression for pick-up at 10:30 or 16:00. The prescription should name the teeth, the number of veneers and the shade.

If the shade needs to be read beside the neighbouring teeth, book a shade visit with Amara Nwosu. The visit fee is €35. The design preview still goes out within two working days, and we mill after approval.

A layered zirconia crown at €145 is a crown with a custom shade, and it stays on the crown line rather than this one.

Inlays and onlays

Inlays and onlays are accepted in ceramic. The fee is €110 for an inlay or an onlay. Send a scan in STL, PLY, OBJ or DCM, or an impression on the courier.

The prescription should name the tooth, say whether the piece is an inlay or an onlay, and give the material and the shade. A design preview is sent within two working days, the same preview rule we use for every case type. The published working-day counts cover single crowns, bridges, veneers, implant crowns and night guards.

They do not state a separate day count for inlays and onlays. Ask cases@hakuji-lab.example about timing for a particular case before you send it, and we will answer from the bench diary rather than from a number the fee list does not carry. The unit fee remains €110.

Implant crowns

Implant crowns are accepted screw-retained or cemented. The fee is €210, and the metal base is included. Turnaround is eight working days, counted from the scan received or from the design approved.

Mei-Lin Hsu works these restorations. Send the scan in STL, PLY, OBJ or DCM. On the prescription, say screw-retained or cemented, name the tooth and give the shade.

We do not accept full-arch implant bars. A single implant crown remains on this list, including a crown that has to sit in a tight space between the arches. The design preview goes out within two working days so the contour can be agreed before anything is milled.

After approval the crown is finished and returned on a weekday courier run. Pick-up at 10:30 and 16:00 is included for practices inside the pick-up area.

Night guards

Night guards are the sixth case type. The fee is €70 for a hard guard or a dual-layer guard. The bench keeps hard and soft splint material for this work.

Turnaround is four working days, counted from the scan received or from the design approved. Rafael Ortiz makes the guards. Send a scan in STL, PLY, OBJ or DCM, or book an impression pick-up.

The prescription should say hard or dual-layer. A design preview is sent within two working days, and finishing starts after you approve it. The finished guard returns on the weekday courier, at 10:30 or 16:00.

Orthodontic appliances are not accepted on this line or on any other. A night guard stays on the night-guard fee. If the prescription is for an orthodontic appliance, we will say so at intake and we will not book it in as a guard.

Work we do not accept

  • Full-arch implant bars
  • Orthodontic appliances
  • Full dentures

Three kinds of work sit outside the six case types. We do not accept full-arch implant bars. We do not accept orthodontic appliances.

We do not accept full dentures. If a prescription arrives for one of those, Sophie Laurent will say so at intake, before design time is spent on it, and we will not invoice a line from the fee table for it. The six types we do accept are single crowns, bridges up to six units, veneers, inlays and onlays, implant crowns and night guards.

An implant crown on its own is accepted. A bar intended to carry a full arch is not. A night guard is accepted.

An orthodontic appliance is not. Send denture work to a laboratory that makes dentures. The phone is (010) 555 0142 if you want that answer before the courier collects a box.

Case stories

Process notes, no outcome claims

01

A four-unit anterior bridge from a scan alone

A practice sent a scan and a prescription for a four-unit anterior bridge, and no impression came with it. Intake checked that the file was STL, PLY, OBJ or DCM, and matched the file name to the prescription. Daniel Okafor built the design, and the preview went back within two working days.

The prescription named four units, inside the six-unit limit, and named zirconia. After the practice approved the preview, Tomas Varga milled the bridge and it moved through finishing. The fee is the zirconia bridge price, €90 per unit.

The working-day count for a bridge is seven, counted from the scan received or from the design approved. The courier returned the box on a weekday pick-up. This note records the path the case took.

It does not record a clinical result.

02

Matching one central incisor after a shade visit

A practice booked a shade visit for one central incisor that needed a custom shade. Amara Nwosu saw the patient in the shade room at Unit 3. The visit fee is €35.

The prescription then named a layered zirconia crown, and Ilse Marchetti layered the porcelain. The unit fee for a layered zirconia crown with a custom shade is €145. The design preview went out within two working days, and the single-crown count is five working days, from the scan received or from the design approved.

The prescription named the tooth, the material and the shade taken at the visit. The shade visit is a record of the tabs read at the window. It is a step in the case.

The remake note elsewhere on this site is the fit policy: a remake for fit asked for within 30 days is at no charge. The note records the charge. It does not record how the first piece sat.

03

An implant crown in a tight space between arches

The prescription was one implant crown in a tight space between the arches, and it asked for a screw-retained crown. Mei-Lin Hsu set the design against the scan the practice sent. The preview showed the contour, and it went out within two working days.

The practice approved that preview, and only then did milling go ahead. The fee is €210, with the metal base included. Turnaround for an implant crown is eight working days, counted from the scan received or from the design approved.

The same fee and the same day count apply when the prescription asks for a cemented crown. We made the crown to the approved design. A remake for fit, if the practice asks within 30 days, is at no charge.

The remake rule states the charge for that window. It does not state how the first piece will sit.

Send us your first case.

Open an account and we will set up your case link, your prescription form and a courier slot. Most practices send a first case within the week they open one, and we reply to every new account within one working day.

Open a lab account

pages.title: Upload guide
pages.content:
Upload

Four steps

Upload guide

Four steps take a case from a new account to a box on the courier. The scan arrives as one of four file types, with a prescription the bench can follow.

Scan, prescribe, approve.

Four steps

01

Open an account

Open an account first. We confirm it within one working day. The message needs the practice name, a contact name, an email, a phone number and the delivery address. Add the registration number if you have it.

02

Export the scan and fill the prescription

Export the scan and fill the prescription. We accept STL, PLY, OBJ and DCM. The prescription should name the case type, the teeth, the material and the shade. If you need a shade visit, say so there.

03

Upload it, or book a pick-up

Upload the file through your case link, or email it to cases@hakuji-lab.example. For a physical impression, book a courier pick-up at 10:30 or 16:00 on a weekday.

04

Approve the design preview

Approve the design preview, which we send within two working days. After that approval we mill, finish and send the work back by courier. The bench does not mill a case before the design is approved.

Four file formats

One scan, one format

STLPLYOBJDCM

Export the surface file your scanner already writes and send one format.

Formats, file names and the prescription

Send STL, PLY, OBJ or DCM. Export the surface file your scanner already writes, and send one format. A second copy in another format is not required.

A photograph of the screen is not a substitute for the file. Name the file with the practice name and the case type, in words. If the case is a single tooth, add the tooth in words.

Leave the patient's name off the file name. Intake uses the name to match the file to the prescription, and the prescription carries the clinical detail. On that prescription, write the case type, the teeth, the material and the shade.

For an implant crown, say screw-retained or cemented. For a bridge, say the number of units, up to six. For a night guard, say hard or dual-layer.

If a shade visit should happen first, write that on the same note.

Impressions, the preview and the next pages

Physical impressions are accepted by courier. Have the box ready for 10:30 or 16:00 on a weekday, inside the pick-up area. The courier fee is included.

Sophie Laurent logs the box at the door. The same prescription fields apply to an impression as to a scan. When the scan is in, we send a design preview within two working days.

Reply with approval, or with the change you want, before we mill. After approval the day count depends on the case: five working days for a single crown, seven for a bridge, six for veneers, eight for an implant crown and four for a night guard, counted from the scan received or from the design approved. Inlays and onlays keep the same preview rule, and the fee is on the fee page.

Accepted cases, the fee table and a new lab account are the three pages that sit next to this guide.

pages.title: Fees
pages.content:
Fees

Per unit, before tax

Fees

Every fee is per unit and before tax. Eight lines cover the work we accept, the night guard and a shade visit at the lab.

Eight lines, per unit, before tax.

Per unit, before tax

ItemWhat is includedFee
Monolithic zirconia crownDesigned, milled, sintered, polished and glazed€95
Layered zirconia crownCustom shade, hand-layered porcelain€145
Lithium disilicate crown or veneerPressed or milled, stained and glazed€125
Zirconia bridge, per unitUp to six units, framework and finish€90
Inlay or onlayCeramic, milled and glazed€110
Implant crownMetal base included, screw-retained or cemented€210
Night guardHard or dual-layer, on a printed model€70
Shade visit at the labAbout forty minutes with a technician€35

Remakes for fit within 30 days are made at no charge. This is a policy, not a guarantee of any clinical result.

A monolithic zirconia crown is €95. A layered zirconia crown, with a custom shade, is €145. A lithium disilicate crown or veneer is €125. A zirconia bridge is €90 per unit, and a bridge may run up to six units.

An inlay or onlay in ceramic is €110. An implant crown is €210, and the metal base is included, whether the crown is screw-retained or cemented. A night guard, hard or dual-layer, is €70. A shade visit at the lab is €35.

Those are the eight lines we invoice. Working days sit beside the prices and are not extra fees. A single crown is five working days, a bridge seven, veneers six, an implant crown eight and a night guard four, counted from the scan received or from the design approved. The design preview, sent within two working days, has no separate charge.

Courier inside the pick-up area has no separate charge either.

Fee notes

Remakes, shade visits, courier

Remakes, shade visits, courier and invoices

A remake for fit within 30 days is at no charge. Ask inside that window and we will remake the unit for fit. The remake is a charge policy for that window.

It covers the fee for the remake. It does not state how the first piece will sit, and it does not state how a restoration will behave in the mouth. A change of shade after you have approved a design is a new instruction.

It is not filed automatically as a remake. The shade visit remains €35 per visit. Saturday visits are by appointment only, between 09:00 and 13:00.

Weekday courier pick-up at 10:30 and at 16:00 is included in the fees for a practice inside the pick-up area. We invoice monthly, in the practice name, using the eight lines above. A question about a line can go to cases@hakuji-lab.example or to (010) 555 0142 during opening hours, Monday to Friday 07:30 to 18:00.

pages.title: Thanks
pages.content:
Thanks

What happens next

Thanks

Your message has left this page. What happens next depends on whether you asked for a lab account, a shade visit, a pick-up or early access to the case portal.

We read it on the next working day.

What happens next

Three things follow an account enquiry. We read it on a working day, Monday to Friday, between 07:30 and 18:00. We confirm the account within one working day when the practice name, contact name, email, phone and delivery address are in the message.

We reply from cases@hakuji-lab.example to the address you gave, with the confirmation or with the one detail still missing. A shade visit and an impression pick-up travel the same route. Shade visits are €35 and, on Saturday, sit between 09:00 and 13:00 by appointment.

Impression pick-ups we can offer are 10:30 and 16:00 on weekdays. If a required field was empty, the reply will name it, and the account clock starts when that detail arrives. The phone, if you would rather speak, is (010) 555 0142.

Early access and the bench letter

If you used the early-access form, your mail app was asked to open a message with the subject Case portal early access. You are not signed up yet. The list starts when that message is sent to cases@hakuji-lab.example.

We reply to the practice email when there is a place. The monthly bench letter covers scans, materials and the pick-up schedule. It does not open a lab account.

An account remains the contact form, or an email whose subject is New lab account. Patient scans should wait for the case path. Please do not attach them to the account form or to the early-access message.

You can return to the home page, the fee table or the upload guide while you wait. Sunday is closed, so a message sent on Sunday is read on Monday from 07:30.

Back to home

pages.title: Privacy
pages.content:
Privacy

Patient data and your questions

Privacy

Scans and prescriptions can identify a patient even when a file name does not. This page says what we receive, who at the bench sees it, and how to ask a question.

Scans can identify a patient.

Patient data in scans

A scan can carry a patient's dental information whether or not a name is written on the file. STL, PLY, OBJ and DCM files, and physical impressions, come to us so we can design and make a restoration. Please do not attach patient scans to the account form.

Once an account exists, send case files by the case link or to cases@hakuji-lab.example in the way the account reply describes. Name a scan file with the practice name and the case type. Leave the patient's name off the file name.

The prescription holds the tooth, the material and the shade. We use these files to prepare a design preview, to mill or layer the work, and to pack the return courier. The people who open a file are those whose role requires it: CAD design, milling and sintering, layering, implant restorations, guards and veneers, shade visits, and case intake.

The account form and your questions

The account form collects the practice name, contact name, email, phone and practice address, and may include a registration number, a request type, expected cases per month, the scanner you use and a message. Consent is required, and it links to this page. Expected cases are recorded as you give them: 1–5, 6–20, or 21 or more.

That figure is your estimate for intake. It is not a quota. We do not sell practice details or scan files, and we do not use case photographs in public notices.

Invoices go out monthly to the practice. A remake request for fit stays with the case through the 30-day window described in the fee notes. To ask what we hold about your practice, email cases@hakuji-lab.example or call (010) 555 0142 in opening hours.

The address is Unit 3, 18 Alder Yard, Westmere. This is the lab's own statement of how case information is handled.

pages.title: Terms
pages.content:
Terms

Accounts, remakes, payment

Terms

These terms cover lab accounts, prescriptions, remakes, liability and payment for work Hakuji Laboratory accepts. They apply to practices sending cases to Unit 3, 18 Alder Yard, Westmere.

The terms for every case.

Accounts and prescriptions

A practice needs an account before we book in a case. We confirm the account within one working day when we have the practice name, contact name, email, phone and delivery address. The registration number may be added when you have it.

Each case needs a prescription naming the case type, the teeth, the material and the shade. An implant crown prescription says screw-retained or cemented. A bridge prescription says the number of units, up to six.

A night guard prescription says hard or dual-layer. We send a design preview within two working days of receiving the scan. Milling, layering and finishing follow your approval of that preview.

The approved design and the prescription are the instructions we make to. A change after approval is a new instruction, and we will say what it does to the day count before we proceed.

Remakes and liability

A remake for fit within 30 days is at no charge. The practice asks inside that window and we remake the unit for fit. The remake is a charge policy for that window.

It covers the fee. It does not state how the first piece will sit, and it does not state how a restoration will perform in the mouth. Shade visits, at €35, record the tabs read in the shade room.

They record the reading. They do not state a visual result. Our responsibility is to make the restoration to the approved design and the prescription, and to return it by the weekday courier.

Day counts are five working days for a single crown, seven for a bridge, six for veneers, eight for an implant crown and four for a night guard, counted from the scan received or from the design approved. Those counts are the planning figures we work to. If we already know of a delay, we tell you.

The counts remain the planning figures, and a delay we have named sits outside them.

Payment and work outside the list

Fees are per unit and before tax. The eight lines are: monolithic zirconia crown €95, layered zirconia crown with a custom shade €145, lithium disilicate crown or veneer €125, zirconia bridge €90 per unit, ceramic inlay or onlay €110, implant crown €210 with the metal base included, night guard hard or dual-layer €70, and shade visit €35. We invoice monthly in the practice name.

Courier pick-up at 10:30 and 16:00 on weekdays is included for practices inside the pick-up area. We do not accept full-arch implant bars, orthodontic appliances or full dentures. If a box arrives for work outside the six case types, we will say so at intake and we will not invoice a fee-table line for it.

Hours for this agreement are Monday to Friday 07:30 to 18:00, Saturday 09:00 to 13:00 for shade visits by appointment only, and Sunday closed. Questions go to cases@hakuji-lab.example or (010) 555 0142.

posts.title: Five habits of a clean scan
posts.excerpt: A short note from the bench on how to send a scan Hakuji Laboratory can design from, in one of the four file formats we accept.
posts.content:
A scan that arrives complete is a scan we can design from. Hakuji Laboratory has made crowns, bridges and implant restorations in Westmere since 2009, and the upload path is short on purpose. This note is the upload guide in brief: five habits we ask of a practice before a file reaches the design screen. The case list is unchanged. We accept single crowns, bridges up to six units, veneers, inlays and onlays, implant crowns and night guards.

The first habit is the file itself. Send STL, PLY, OBJ or DCM. Those are the four formats the lab accepts. Export the surface file your scanner already writes, and send one of them. A photograph of a monitor, or a picture of a model, cannot take the place of that file. If the only record you hold is a physical impression, leave it as an impression. Book a courier pick-up and Sophie Laurent will take the box at the door. Collections run at 10:30 and at 16:00 on weekdays, inside the pick-up area, and the courier is included in the fee.

The second habit is the file name. Use the practice name and the case type, in words. If the case is a single tooth, add the tooth in words as well. Leave the patient's name off the file name. The prescription holds the clinical detail, and the file name only has to help intake match the file to that prescription. One clear name is enough. Sending the same case as STL and again as PLY and again as OBJ slows the morning, and the extra copies do not change the design we prepare.

The third habit is the prescription that travels with the file. Name the case type and the teeth. Name the material: monolithic zirconia, layered zirconia, lithium disilicate, ceramic for an inlay or onlay, or a hard or dual-layer night guard. Name the shade. For an implant crown, say whether it is screw-retained or cemented. For a bridge, say the number of units, and keep the span to six or fewer. If you want a shade visit before a custom shade is layered, write that on the prescription. The visit is €35 at the lab, by appointment, with Amara Nwosu. Ilse Marchetti layers the porcelain for a custom-shade zirconia crown, and that crown is €145.

The fourth habit is what the scan shows. Include the preparation and the neighbouring teeth the case has to sit among. A bridge needs the preparations the unit count refers to. A veneer needs the teeth named on the prescription. An implant crown needs the record you want the design set against, including the space between the arches when that space is the reason for the case. A scan cropped to a single stump, with the neighbours cut away, leaves contact and shade without a reference. Send a plain, complete arch rather than a tightly cropped one. Use the ordinary export your scanner offers for STL, PLY, OBJ or DCM. No extra setting is required beyond that file.

The fifth habit is the way the file comes in, and what you should expect afterwards. Open an account first if you do not yet have one. We confirm it within one working day. Then upload through your case link, or email the file to cases@hakuji-lab.example. Please do not attach patient scans to the public account form. When the file is in, Daniel Okafor's side of the bench sends a design preview within two working days. Milling, layering and finishing start after you approve that preview. A single crown is five working days, a bridge seven, veneers six, an implant crown eight and a night guard four, counted from the scan received or from the design approved. An inlay or onlay follows the same preview habit, and the fee is €110.

The bench opens at 07:30. Design previews that are ready go out at 13:00. The lab closes at 18:00 on weekdays. Saturday, from 09:00 to 13:00, is for shade visits by appointment, and Sunday is closed. If a file will miss the morning collection, the next weekday run is at 16:00. A clean scan is a file we can open, a name we can match to a prescription, and a design you can approve before anything is milled. Fees stay on the fee page, from €70 for a night guard to €210 for an implant crown with the metal base included, all per unit and before tax. That is the upload guide in one note from the bench.

The materials note records that the bench keeps a layered zirconia shade set for custom-shade crowns. Ilse Marchetti layers that porcelain. The fee for a layered zirconia crown with a custom shade is €145, before tax, per unit.

Where the shade needs to be read at the lab, the practice books a shade visit with Amara Nwosu. The visit is €35, by appointment, and Saturday visits fall between 09:00 and 13:00. The note does not add a new case type and it does not change the five-working-day count for a single crown.

A monolithic zirconia crown remains €95 when a custom layer is not required. Lithium disilicate, at €125 for a crown or a veneer, is unchanged. The tag on the note is materials.

posts.content:
The schedule note is where we tell practices which collections still run when a week is short. The standing pick-ups stay 10:30 and 16:00 on weekdays the lab is open, and those collections are included in the fees inside the pick-up area. Opening hours remain Monday to Friday 07:30 to 18:00.

Saturday is 09:00 to 13:00 for shade visits by appointment only. Sunday is closed. The note does not create a second courier price, and it does not move the design-preview rule: a preview still goes out within two working days of a scan we have received.

If a case has to leave before a short week, call (010) 555 0142 before the 10:30 collection and Sophie Laurent will say which run can take the box. The tag on the note is schedule. Fee lines stay on the fees page.
